headline: Defence Adviser: Armed forces will remain politically neutral, professional
summary: Brig Gen (retd) Dr AKM Shamsul Islam pledges that merit-based promotions and accountability for human rights violations will be guide the military's future.
details: Defence Adviser Brig Gen (retd) Dr AKM Shamsul Islam stated that the government will not allow the armed forces to be used as a partisan political instrument, ensuring they remain a professional and people-oriented force.
Speaking at a RAOWA event in Mohakhali, he emphasized that merit and competence will be the only criteria for promotion and assignment of responsibilities within the military.
The adviser warned that no special protection will be provided to those involved in enforced disappearances or killings, and every individual will be held accountable for their actions.
He noted that the government is working to restore the dignity of officers who were persecuted during the previous administration and is committed to modernizing the country's defense capabilities.
Shamsul Islam also pledged continued support for the rehabilitation and treatment of injured July fighters, with some severe cases being sent abroad for advanced medical care.
A presentation by the July Shaheed Smriti Foundation revealed that 15,903 people were injured during the uprising, with 43 losing their eyesight and 2,000 losing their ability to work.
The foundation has distributed Tk 117 crore among 831 families of martyrs and 8,117 injured people, but requires another Tk 263 crore to support remaining beneficiaries.
The adviser further committed to ensuring justice for the killing of retired army major Sinha Mohammad Rashed Khan and implementing commission recommendations.
caption:
The armed forces belong to the people, not to a political party. Defence Adviser Shamsul Islam pledges a neutral, merit-based military.

Defence Adviser Brig Gen (retd) Dr AKM Shamsul Islam stated that the government will not allow the armed forces to be used as a partisan political instrument, ensuring they remain a professional and people-oriented force.

Speaking at a RAOWA event in Mohakhali, he emphasized that merit and competence will be the only criteria for promotion and assignment of responsibilities within the military.

The adviser warned that no special protection will be provided to those involved in enforced disappearances or killings, and every individual will be held accountable for their actions.

He noted that the government is working to restore the dignity of officers who were persecuted during the previous administration and is committed to modernizing the country's defense capabilities.

Shamsul Islam also pledged continued support for the rehabilitation and treatment of injured July fighters, with some severe cases being sent abroad for advanced medical care.

A presentation by the July Shaheed Smriti Foundation revealed that 15,903 people were injured during the uprising, with 43 losing their eyesight and 2,000 losing their ability to work.

The foundation has distributed Tk 117 crore among 831 families of martyrs and 8,117 injured people, but requires another Tk 263 crore to support remaining beneficiaries.

The adviser further committed to ensuring justice for the killing of retired army major Sinha Mohammad Rashed Khan and implementing commission recommendations.

headline: Law minister says extrajudicial killings have almost dropped to zero
summary: The Law Minister of Bangladesh has stated that incidents of extrajudicial killings in the country have nearly vanished.
details: The Law Minister of Bangladesh has claimed that extrajudicial killings in the country have almost dropped to zero.
This statement comes as part of a broader discussion on the state of law and order and human rights in the country.
The minister's claim suggests a significant reduction in such incidents, reflecting the government's commitment to legal processes.
The statement has been made during a a public address or official event, highlighting the government's position on the law enforcement's conduct.
